What if one sharp corner could tear a jet in half?
In 1952, the Comet became the world's first jet airliner.
It flew higher and faster than any passenger plane before it.
But in 1954, two Comets broke apart in mid-air, just three months apart.
So engineers sank a whole Comet in a giant water tank.
They pumped the cabin up and let it down, again and again, like flight after flight.
After about three thousand cycles, it ripped open.
The crack began at the sharp corner of a cabin opening.
Every flight, stress piled up at those corners, and tiny cracks grew a little longer.
A rounded corner lets that stress flow smoothly around the curve.
That's why every plane window you've ever looked through is round.
